class_guess: Bouncer + Chaotic Edge; twin of #13 at the cycle level (same bulk, junction and tail orbit D_n)
summary: #13's twin: same period-10 bouncer, same 7 junction words, same chaotic tail D_n cycle for cycle. Tail = whole problem.
mechanism: Bulk (1101101101)^a on a left wall moves 1 cell left per bounce (62a steps); the junction cycles through #13's 7 words; 1 bounce in 7 touches the tail D.
D_n equals #13's D_n in all 1,952 shared cycles, and the probe map P is #13's (217/217 tested, 0 disagree). #35 = this table renamed; #34 = #13 mirrored.
Halt only via B reading 0 with 00 on its left. Never seen: the edge map is clean to 1.5e7 cycles (about 4.9e16 steps). The tail has no proof.

template.note: sideRLs: a fixed crossing protocol into a one-sided right part fits (ours: 14 fixed round trips 2 cells left of the X0|D cut), but TM1's RC i is an explicit word; our D is chaotic and needs a closed language (#13's lemma E'). The A-C neighbours in RWL_mod_v2.v / CPS_LRU_v1.v are decider certificates: same parameters give false here.

strategy: Everything except the edge is routine (Bouncer_v3/sideRLs shape; init by direct execution, 657,139 steps). A kill needs #13's edge lemma (E'): a closed language for D under P. It is shared by #13, #34, #35 and #36, so one lemma would mean 4 kills. Until then, park with #13.
risks: Edge lemma open: #13 refuted SFT_k invariants for k <= 36 and plain n-gram CPS (n <= 26); no regular invariant is known.
mxdys listed the family on UBRRBA_TODO (a halting tool): a late break or halt is possible; edge map clean to 1.5e7 cycles (about 4.9e16 steps).
Even with (E'), this machine needs its own .v: same architecture, but the wall, the sweeps (62a) and the step constants differ from #13.
